task:
The unnest_subqueries optimizer rule, and so optimizer.optimize, changes query results when a subquery sits in a JOIN ON clause. It moves the condition to WHERE, or it hoists the subquery, even when that changes which rows survive.

Example: SELECT x.a FROM x LEFT JOIN y ON x.a = y.b AND y.b IN (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = 2) keeps every row of x. After the rewrite, a WHERE ... IS NOT NULL drops rows of x. An inner join predicate under OR or NOT also gets replaced by TRUE, which inverts or widens it.

unnest_subqueries must leave each query below exactly as written:

- An IN subquery in the ON of a LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, SEMI or ANTI join, with the ON above.
- SELECT x.a FROM x JOIN y ON x.a = y.b OR y.b IN (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b > 100)
- SELECT x.a FROM x JOIN y ON NOT (y.b = ANY (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b > 100))
- SELECT x.a FROM x LEFT JOIN y ON y.b = (SELECT MAX(z.b) AS b FROM y AS z)
- SELECT x.a FROM x LEFT JOIN y ON y.b = (SELECT MAX(z.b) AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = x.a)
- SELECT x.a FROM x JOIN y ON x.a = (SELECT MAX(z.b) AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = y.b). The subquery refers to y, the table being joined, which is not yet available before the join.
- SELECT x.a, w.d FROM x JOIN y ON x.a = y.b AND y.b IN (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = 2) RIGHT JOIN w ON FALSE, and the same with FULL JOIN in place of RIGHT JOIN. A later RIGHT or FULL join keeps rows that a moved WHERE would drop.

The general rules. An uncorrelated subquery in an ON clause may be rewritten only if it is an IN or = ANY predicate, it is a top-level conjunct of the ON, through AND and parentheses only, it sits on a plain or INNER join of the current select, with no side, method or match condition, and no RIGHT or FULL join follows. An uncorrelated scalar subquery in any ON stays. A correlated subquery in an ON may be rewritten only on such a plain inner join with an ON, and only if all its outer columns come from sources before that join.

These must still be rewritten, with this exact output:

- SELECT x.a FROM x INNER JOIN y ON x.a = y.b AND (y.b IN (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = 2)) becomes SELECT x.a FROM x INNER JOIN y ON x.a = y.b AND (TRUE) LEFT JOIN (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = 2 GROUP BY z.b) AS _u_0 ON y.b = _u_0.b WHERE NOT _u_0.b IS NULL
- SELECT x.a FROM x JOIN y ON x.a = y.b AND y.b = ANY (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = 2) becomes SELECT x.a FROM x JOIN y ON x.a = y.b AND TRUE LEFT JOIN (SELECT z.b AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = 2 GROUP BY z.b) AS _u_0 ON y.b = _u_0.b WHERE NOT _u_0.b IS NULL
- SELECT x.a FROM x JOIN y ON y.b = (SELECT MAX(z.b) AS b FROM y AS z WHERE z.b = x.a) ORDER BY x.a becomes SELECT x.a FROM x LEFT JOIN (SELECT MAX(z.b) AS b, z.b AS _u_1 FROM y AS z WHERE TRUE GROUP BY z.b) AS _u_0 ON _u_0._u_1 = x.a JOIN y ON y.b = _u_0.b ORDER BY x.a

The full optimize pipeline must follow the same rules. A LEFT JOIN with ON a.id = c.id AND c.domain IN (SELECT ...) must come out with the IN subquery still inside the ON, with no extra CTE and no WHERE. Results of each query on real data must match before and after optimize, in DuckDB, for the LEFT JOIN IN, the OR, and both LEFT JOIN scalar cases, with columns x.a and y.b selected.

Everything else must keep working.
